title: Pokémon Go teams up with Crocs and Duolingo for a pair of crossover events
summary: A brand named after a crocodile and an app with an owl for a mascot don’t sound like natural Pokémon Go partners, though Totodile and Hoothoot might have a few things to say about that, what with Crocs avatar items out around the world from today and Duolingo’s second crossover starting on November 17th! The Crocs side is avatar items based on its Pokémon collection, and there are three of them: the Pikachu Classic Clog, the Gengar Classic Clog and the Jigglypuff Classic Platform Clog. Pikachu’s is the easy one, as you just enter the code POKEMONGOxCROCSxELECTRIFYING on the Pokémon Go Web Store and the item’s yours.  ... [MORE]

title: Rogue Adventure offers classic, no-frills roguelike deckbuilding fun, finally on iOS
summary: Roguelike deckbuilder, roguelike deckbuilder, roguelike deckbuilder. A genre so storied that, even a few years after being invented, it recently got an entire game riffing on the title alone. But that doesn't mean it's devoid of the fun like all good trends eventually are, especially with Rogue Adventure now available on iOS! Originally released back in 2019, Rogue Adventure is a roguelike deckbuilder (see?) that has you picking from over 200 different cards as you journey across a fantasy land, doing battle with various monsters and enemies. You'll have 16 classes with different starting decks to choose from, four distinct modes and even weekly tournaments to test your mettle in. All this, and more than seven years of updates and fixes too. ... [MORE]

title: Gravemark is a roguelike dungeon crawler you can play in portrait mode, out now on iOS
summary: Ever since 198X's Rogue, the idea of venturing into a dungeon, grabbing loot and attempting to exit without being killed has thrilled hardcore players. No surprise then, that Gravemark, a portrait-mode roguelike, has really caught our eye. And now it's not just Android players able to enjoy it, as Gravemark hits iOS! At its core, Gravemark is your stereotypical roguelike. Venture into the deep dungeon, automatically battle enemies while selecting skills and potions, then decide what to put into your limited inventory space before choosing whether to plunge deeper or get out. The twists are the aforementioned auto-battles, limited inventory, and the fact you don't actually know what the loot is until you take it back to be identified. ... [MORE]

title: Gudnak Digital is a deck-based strategy game coming to mobile that surprisingly ISN'T European
summary: The tabletop-to-digital pipeline is a tried-and-true method of bringing new and exciting games to mobile. And now, developer Chaotic Great are set to step onto iOS and Android with their roguelike deck-building strategy game Gudnak Digital! Arriving December 1st, it gives you the freedom to make strategic decisions, no matter how ill-advised. Tongue-in-cheek tagline aside, Gudnak Digital takes you to a fantastical world orbiting a dying sun. With the planet slowly cooling and everyone, understandably, unhappy about the subject, factions are pitted against one another in constant battle to overwhelm the other as they duke it out on the field of warfare. ... [MORE]

title: Lil’ Guardsman puts a twelve-year-old in charge of a fantasy kingdom's border control
summary: Lil’ Guardsman is out now on iOS and Android, and you’re playing a twelve-year-old called Lil who’s been left on gate duty. Her dad’s gone off and left her in charge, and she’s not too thrilled about it. Can’t say I blame her. Everyone who rocks up at the guard shed is her call: in, out or the dungeon. It’s border control with goblins and elves in the queue, played for laughs. You question whoever shows up, and what you say counts, and the Truth Spray and the Metal Detector help you work out who’s lying, along with a Whip, which I wasn’t expecting to see handed to a twelve-year-old. ... [MORE]

title: Where Winds Meet challenges you with tough choices in its 1st anniversary update
summary: Where Winds Meet and its sprawling Wuxia storyline have explored all manner of drama and action, and now you'll be faced with your toughest choices yet in their new update. As the 1st anniversary of Where Winds Meet arrives, alongside the Hutuo region, your adherence to Xia (the martial code of justice) is going to be tested like never before. The Hutuo region itself represents a dramatically different place from the far west that's been explored in previous updates. This riverside region features its own campaign that pits you against the armoured general Xiao Han, as well as exploring the idea of what Xia's true meaning is in three new storylines delving into the effects of the ongoing conflict. ... [MORE]

title: Minami Co. offers incremental gameplay with a maid spin and a big asterisk
summary: While we've had roguelikes, Balatro-likes and Survivors-likes all making waves on mobile, the humble incremental game remains a best-selling genre. Now, you can hop into another number-building adventure with the launch of Minami Co. for Android! Minami Co. sees you playing as Kasumi Minami, who inherits a safety pin factory from her late father. As the new CEO, it's your job to print out new pins with exciting designs and slowly grow your factory from a small workshop into a sprawling production line. Along the way, your family, consisting of your Mom and sisters Rin and Yuzu, will help further upgrade and expand until, like any good incremental game, the numbers are sky-high! ... [MORE]

title: Solitaire(ish) turns classic card stacking into a roguelike for Apple Arcade
summary: solitaire(ish) is the new one from Playstack, the publisher behind Balatro, and it’s coming to Apple Arcade next month. So, Solitaire. But a roguelike, and made in-house at Playstack Leeds. There’s a boss too, a King, and he’s allowed to change the rules on you whenever he likes (reverse stacking included, which sounds properly nasty). Most of it you’ll already know. Descending order, red on black, black on red, same as ever. Now every stack scores, though, and there’s a target to hit that keeps climbing each round. You earn cash along the way and spend it in the shop, where Switchers are the simple option, letting you swap the rank or colour of a card that’s already down. ... [MORE]

title: Loco Motive is bringing its comedy murder mystery to iOS in 2027
summary: Point-and-click adventures have always suited touchscreens, since tapping on things is most of what you do in them anyway. So, it’s good news that Loco Motive, the comedy murder mystery, is in development for iOS, with a release planned for some point in 2027. The news came out alongside the Hands On update for the PC version, which marks its second anniversary and adds full touch controls on Steam Deck. You can switch between touch, a controller and a mouse at any point, which is probably a decent sign for how it’ll play on a phone. Chucklefish says more details on the iOS version will follow. ... [MORE]

title: The Red Cathedral brings its competitive cathedral-building board game to iOS and Android
summary: It’s been a little while coming, but Devir’s digital edition of The Red Cathedral is finally out on iOS and Android (and on PC through Steam, for that matter). I wrote about it back when it was first announced in May, and Iwan had another look in September once it got a release date, so we’ve been keeping tabs on this one for most of the year. You’re after the Tsar’s favour - Ivan the Terrible, no less, and so is everyone else at the table. Up to four of you are chipping in on the same cathedral, though each of you has claimed your own bits of it, and you need to go and find the materials to actually build those bits and then decorate them. The clergy and the city’s guilds come into it too. Whoever’s racked up the most prestige by the time the whole thing is finished wins. ... [MORE]

title: Little Library brings village life sim and bookshop management to iOS and Android this November
summary: Only a few weeks after Kettle Street gave you a bare flat and a list of odd jobs around Kettleby, another cosy life sim is handing you a struggling village to help out. Little Library launches on iOS and Android later this month, and the village in question is Maplewood, which has just got itself a brand-new library and not a lot of money to run it with. Keeping the doors open is on you. There’s a small budget to stretch between new books and putting on events, and every time someone walks in, you’ll have to play librarian and work out what they want to read.  ... [MORE]

title: Feed the Scorchpot serves up a dice-rolling roguelike where you cook for a dragon
summary: Feed the Scorchpot is based on a rather simple deal - a dragon protects your island for twenty years, and in return, you cook it dinner for twenty years. The hand-drawn dice roguelike from husband-and-wife studio Moravian is out now in early access on Google Play, with an iOS version coming soon. Each year, you roll dice to work the island, harvest ingredients, combine them into recipes and then cook them down in the Scorchpot itself. If the meal isn’t up to scratch, then it’s been made fairly clear that you end up in the pot instead. ... [MORE]

title: Clone Drone in the Danger Zone finally brings its limb-slicing combat to mobile
summary: We’ve been keeping a close eye on Clone Drone in the Danger Zone since it was first announced for mobile. And now, the voxel-based hack ‘n slash finally launched on iOS and Android. On top of that, the studio has marked the occasion with a 10-year Anniversary Update as well. title: Torchlight: Infinite brings back its permadeath server as Assassin's Creed crossover looms
summary: My first question when I heard that Torchlight: Infinite was getting an Assassin’s Creed crossover was whether anyone had thought about the practicalities. All those hooded assassins, all those monsters, and not a haystack in sight. Ubisoft's finest are going to have to improvise. The collaboration is confirmed for January 2027, with more details expected over the coming weeks.  There's something a little more immediate to get sucked into, though. The Unbound, Torchlight: Infinite's hardcore server, has returned with the arrival of SS14 Tartarus. First introduced during SS13 Afterlight last summer, it gives you a fresh start with the rather significant caveat that death is permanent. Make it through and you'll be chasing better rewards and a spot on the leaderboards. Make one mistake, and well, there's always next season. ... [MORE]

title: Warhammer Survivors reveals its roadmap, with new characters, weapons and cross-save on the way
summary: One of my colleagues gave Warhammer Survivors a go this week and lasted about a minute before a stampede of rats ran them over. The weekend has since been set aside for revenge. Good timing, because Auroch Digital has just revealed a roadmap for the Survivors-like, which is out now on iOS and Android, and there’s a lot more on the way to die to. Most of the roadmap includes free updates over the next few months, adding new characters and weapons to both the Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar halves, along with QoL fixes. Smaller patches will fill the gaps between the bigger drops, with some of them landing before the end of the year.  ... [MORE]

Case in point: the seismic reaction to Poppy Playtime Chapter Five, which sold 110,000 copies in only three hours on PC, and which has now finally landed on iOS and Android! If you're not familiar, Poppy Playtime sees you delving into the ruined toy factory of Playtime Co., and unsurprisingly the enormous, spooky abandoned industrial relic turns out to be hosting a lot more than just asbestos and still water, with the vicious Huggy Wuggy (yes, really) dogging your steps as you delve further, and further, into the depths of the factory. ... [MORE]

title: Asphalt Legends sees iconic car manufacturer Ferrari get its own dedicated season
summary: Asphalt Legends Unite has covered some of the most famous automobile brands of all time. But one of their most well-known partnerships has been with none other than Ferrari. Now, the iconic Italian manufacturer is receiving its own dedicated season in Asphalt Legends! Ferrari Season, which runs until December 9th, introduces three new iconic cars to the track in Asphalt Legends. Currently, the Ferrari F800 has the spotlight, while the Ferrari 849 Testarossa arrives until November 25th, and the Ferrari 296 GT3 Evo until December 2nd. All of these cars are faithfully recreated from their real-world counterparts down to the smallest detail. ... [MORE]

title: PUBG Mobile Flash puts the battleground in the palm of your hand at less than 1 GB
summary: One of the biggest pain points for gaming nowadays is download size. And on mobile, especially if you're playing via data roaming, that's doubly true. Fortunately, if you're in need of a quick game, PUBG Mobile Flash puts the battleground in the palm of your hand lickety-split! As you might expect from the name (previously called PUBG Mobile Light), this is a stripped-down version of the original PUBG Mobile. Featuring the main map of Erangel and classic Battle Royale mode, both preinstalled. In total, this download size comes down to a minuscule 1 GB on Android and 2 GB on iOS! ... [MORE]

title: Umamusume: Pretty Derby teams up with the F1 Japanese Grand Prix 2027
summary: With its mixture of over-the-top musical numbers, adorable horse girl antics and genuinely thrilling race-day action, Umamusume: Pretty Derby has shot to fame all over the world. But nowhere else is it more popular than in its native Japan, especially as Umamusume: Pretty Derby is partnering with the 2027 F1 Japan Grand Prix. The partnership saw developer and publisher Cygames become a Founding Partner for the 2027 iteration of the competition, as well as getting naming rights to Suzuka Circuit's 130R corner. Naturally, this part of the track, which is well-known for its sharp turn, will be known as Umamusume 130R. ... [MORE]

title: Inside is a moody, critically acclaimed little indie platformer, coming to Android
summary: With all the big, flashy games releasing on mobile lately, you may have missed a humble but critically acclaimed game set to launch on Android. Yes, Playdead's seminal indie platformer Inside is coming to Android, with pre-registration now open so you can find out exactly what all the fuss has been about. In Inside, you play as a young boy in a world of technological horror, evading various hazards in your quest to find out what exactly is going on. Like Playdead's most famous game, Limbo, it's a moody, monochrome platformer that has you exploring a winding world of surreal and frightening imagery. ... [MORE]
